sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:46033
Court No. - 82
Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 6536 of 2023

Revisionist :- Juvenile -X
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Revisionist :- Anil Kumar Dubey

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.
Heard Sri A.K. Dubey, learned counsel for the revisionist and Sri R.K. Verma, learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.This criminal revision has been filed for setting aside the judgment and order dated 11.08.2023 passed by Juvenile Justice Board, Pilibhit and order dated 21.10.2023, passed by Special Judge (POCSO Act)/Juvenile Judge, Pilibhit, in Criminal Appeal No. 68 of 2023, affirming the order of J.
J. Board declining bail to the juvenile in Case Crime No. 246 of 2023 under Sections 307 and 376-D I.P.C. and section 5/6 of POCSO Act, P.S.- Pooranpur, District- Pilibhit.
3. As per the version in the F.I.R., a 17 year old daughter was attacked by some unknown person on her neck and she became seriously injured and unconscious.
She was hospitalized and her family members waited for her to regain consciousness.
A case crime no. 0246 of 2023 was lodged under section 307 I.P.C. against an unknown person.

Later on, statements of the victim under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. were recorded where she disclosed that she was attacked by co-accused Fariyad and that she was sexually assaulted by the co-accused as well as the instant juvenile.

She was put to Juvenile -X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 14 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5645063/
1 medical examination.

entities.text: Juvenile -X vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the medical opinion no internal or external injury was found on her private parts, however, injury was found on her neck.
Finding the accused involved in the matter below 18 years of age, he was produced before the J.J. Board.
The application moved on his behalf for his release into care and custody of his father was rejected.
The appeal preferred challenging the order of the J.J. Board
was also dismissed declining him bail.
4. It is contended on behalf of the revisionist that he has been falsely implicated for some ulterior motives.
On the date of incident he was not around the place of occurrence.

The allegation of causing injury on the neck has been imputed on co-accused- Fariyad only and that he has already been released on bail vide order dated 24.07.2023 in Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 32069 of 2023.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 32069 of 2023
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: There is no allegation of against the juvenile of causing any injury.
He is found aged 13 years only and that he has already been detained in juvenile home since 23.05.2023 i.e. about 10 months now.
It is argued that considering the tender age of the accused he should have released in the care and custody of his parents so that his good care be taken.
Further contention of the revisionist is that nothing material was found in the social investigation report so as to dissuade the J.J. Board and the appellate court from granting him bail.
It is argued that the J.J. Board as well as the appellate court have conveniently ignored the settled principles of law while declining him bail.
In fact bail to the juvenile has been refused on the basis of the inferences drawn without having any material to substantiate them therefore, such orders are unsustainable in law.
5. Learned A.G.A has opposed prayer for bail.
However, most of the factual situation as mentioned above could not be refuted.
6. I went through the contents of the F.I.R., statements given by the victim and the social investigation report.

There is no material observation as regard his conduct, behaviour or antecedents which may have counted with the court or the J.J. Board to bring the matter of grant of bail within the three exceptional circumstances as provided in proviso to section 12 of the J.J. Act,
2015.

In fact, there is no material which, in my view, could have dissuaded the court or the J.J.
Board from granting bail or release to his parents.

The settled law is that whenever a minor, who is alleged to have committed an offence, is apprehended and produced before the board, he shall be released on bail unless the release is likely to bring him in association with any known criminal or there is likelihood of exposure to moral or psychological danger or that such release would defeat ends of justice.

7. In view of the above, the revision is allowed and the order dated dated 11.08.2023, passed by the J.J. Board in Case Crime No. 246 of 2023 under Sections 307 and 376-D I.P.C. and section 5/6 of POCSO Act, P.S.- Pooranpur, District- Pilibhit and order dated 21.10.2023, passed by the appellate court in Criminal Appeal No. 68 of 2023, are hereby set aside.

sentences.text: It is made clear that the observations made in this order are limited to the purpose of determination of this bail application and will in no way be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
The trial court/J.J.Board shall be absolutely free to arrive at its independent conclusions on the basis of evidence led, uninfluenced by any finding or observation whatsoever in this order.
